title: Locally constant geometric component counts for proper flat algebraic spaces
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $h:Y\to T$ a morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $h$ is proper, flat, and of finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Here finite presentation means local finite presentation on etale scheme charts, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (quasi-compact diagonal). Suppose that every geometric fibre is reduced: each etale scheme chart of $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, for every algebraically closed field-valued point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], has reduced local rings. For $t\in T$, choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ of its residue field [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $n(t)$ be the number of connected components of $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}$, with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A connected component is a maximal nonempty connected subset. Then $n(t)$ is finite and independent of the chosen algebraic closure; $n:T\to\mathbf N$ is locally constant, meaning every point has an open neighbourhood on which $n$ is constant. The same number is obtained using any algebraically closed extension of $\kappa(t)$. Empty fibres have $n(t)=0$, and $n(t)=1$ if and only if $Y_t$ is geometrically connected: after every extension of $\kappa(t)$ its point space is nonempty and connected. In particular the locus of nonempty geometrically connected fibres is open in $T$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $T$, smoothness hypothesis on $h$, or representability of $h$ by schemes is required.

proof.text: Fix $t$, put $k=\kappa(t)$ and $Z=Y_t$. For two algebraically closed extensions $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ of $k$, choose a common extension field and then its algebraic closure $M$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $(Z_{\Omega_i})_M$ with $Z_M$. The separably closed component theorem applied over each algebraically closed $\Omega_i$ gives bijections $\pi_0(Z_{\Omega_i})\simeq\pi_0(Z_M)$. Thus the component count is independent of the algebraic closure, and agrees with the count over every algebraically closed extension.

Properness survives base change, so $Y_{\bar t}$ is proper over the chosen algebraically closed residue field. It is reduced by hypothesis. The global-algebra component theorem therefore gives finitely many clopen components and $\Gamma(Y_{\bar t},\mathcal O)=\overline{\kappa(t)}^{\pi_0(Y_{\bar t})}$. Its vector-space dimension is exactly $n(t)$, including dimension zero for an empty fibre.

source.place: Tag 0E1E, lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, identification of n with beta_0; spaces-over-fields Tag 0DMY(1)--(3).

proof.text: Apply proper-flat derived base change to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Y$: it is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank one on $Y$, hence finitely presented, and is flat over $T$ because $h$ is flat. Obtain the perfect Zariski complex $K=R\epsilon_{T,*}Rh_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_Y$. For $i_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$, base change identifies $Li_t^*K$ with the derived fibre direct image. Degree zero is $\Gamma(Y_t,\mathcal O)$: in a nonnegative injective resolution, left exactness identifies the kernel in degree zero with ordinary sections. The same applies after extending $\kappa(t)$ to any field. Thus $\beta_0(K,t)$ is fibrewise $h^0$; it is finite, since a perfect complex over a field is represented by a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces.

source.place: Tag 0CTM, lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general, and Tag 0E0R, lemma-jump-loci-geometric, proof, with the structure sheaf.

proof.text: The perfect jump-loci theorem makes $\beta_0(K,-)$ upper semicontinuous and invariant under base change. Base change to $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ and steps 2--3 give $\beta_0(K,t)=n(t)$. The lower-semicontinuity theorem applies to $h$ without any reducedness assumption. At a fixed $t$ choose an open $V$ where $n(u)\ge n(t)$ and an open $W$ where $\beta_0(K,u)\le\beta_0(K,t)$; the latter is the open sublevel set $\{\beta_0<n(t)+1\}$. On $V\cap W$, the two inequalities give $n(u)=n(t)$. Hence $n$ is locally constant.

proof.text: A space with exactly one nonempty connected component is nonempty and connected, since its components cover it. Suppose $n(t)=1$. The separably closed component theorem says that $Z_{\bar k}$ remains connected after every extension of $\bar k$. Given any $L/k$, embed $L$ and $\bar k$ in a common field $M$; then $Z_M$ is connected. The map $|Z_M|\to|Z_L|$ is continuous by the point calculus and surjective: the point-image formula for $Z_L\times_L\operatorname{Spec}M$ gives the whole target because $|\operatorname{Spec}M|\to|\operatorname{Spec}L|$ is onto. A continuous surjective image of a nonempty connected space is connected: a separation downstairs would pull back to a separation upstairs. Thus every $Z_L$ is nonempty and connected. Conversely geometric connectedness includes connectedness of $Z_{\bar k}$, so its component count is one. For an empty fibre the component set is empty and its count is zero.

The locus in question is $n^{-1}(\{1\})$. Each of its points has, by local constancy, an open neighbourhood contained in that locus, so it is open. All inputs above have precisely the stated finite-presentation and flatness hypotheses; none requires a Noetherian base, smoothness, or a scheme source.

lean.statement: theorem proper_flat_geometric_component_count {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : Over S) (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : Y ⟶ schemeSpace T) (hproper : MapIsProper h) (hflat : MapIsFlat h) (hlfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation h) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact h.hom.hom) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal h.hom.hom)) (hred : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (a : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T.left) (U : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Limits.pullback h.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (a ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) a rfl))), IsEtale b → ∀ x : U.left, _root_.IsReduced (U.left.presheaf.stalk x)) : ∃ n : T.left → ℕ, (∀ (t : T.left) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (ι : T.left.residueField t ⟶ CommRingCat.of Ω), Finite (ConnectedComponents (Point (Limits.pullback h.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk ((Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) (Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) rfl))))) ∧ Nat.card (ConnectedComponents (Point (Limits.pullback h.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk ((Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) (Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) rfl))))) = n t) ∧ IsLocallyConstant n ∧ (∀ t : T.left, IsEmpty (Point (Limits.pullback h.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) rfl)))) → n t = 0) ∧ (∀ t : T.left, n t = 1 ↔ ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] (ι : T.left.residueField t ⟶ CommRingCat.of L), ConnectedSpace (Point (Limits.pullback h.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk ((Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) (Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) rfl))))) ∧ IsOpen {t : T.left | ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] (ι : T.left.residueField t ⟶ CommRingCat.of L), ConnectedSpace (Point (Limits.pullback h.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk ((Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) (Spec.map ι ≫ T.left.fromSpecResidueField t) rfl))))}
